h1: The Salil Thonglor — a British-style boutique in the heart of Bangkok's most stylish district
intro: Step into Soi Sukhumvit 57, just a few steps from BTS Thong Lo, and you find a white building dressed in vintage British detail — The Salil Hotel Sukhumvit 57 - Thonglor, a boutique that blends English-colonial atmosphere with a contemporary edge. Opened in 2017 with 130 rooms, a Mariage Frères tea room and a rooftop pool people love to photograph, it sits right in Thonglor, one of the city's most fashionable neighbourhoods for food and cafés. Rooms start from approx. THB 2,800/night, with a score of 8.9 from 1,214 reviews on Trip.com.

body.html: The Salil Thonglor positioned itself as a 'lifestyle' hotel from the start, and what people remember most is its carefully detailed vintage-British design — floral wallpaper, dark wood furniture, brass lamps and corners that look like they belong in a London townhouse. It has been open since 2017 but remains well kept, and is one of the boutiques that comes up most often when people think of where to stay in Thonglor.

Its 130 rooms start with the Premier Room at around 30 sqm and rise to the 45 sqm Living Suite — nearly all of them have a fridge and a small kitchenette, handy for longer stays or for bringing snacks back to the room. Many reviews say the rooms are larger than expected for the price and the beds comfortable. A recurring note is that some rooms are starting to show wear and the décor leans classic compared with newer boutiques.
"The room was just as pretty as the photos, every corner is a photo op, the staff were lovely, and BTS Thong Lo is a few minutes' walk — great value for what we paid."

The part reviews mention most is the rooftop pool on the 8th floor, with views over Thonglor. It isn't large, but the atmosphere is lovely for an evening dip and photos. Downstairs there's Bar Storia del Café serving coffee and all-day dining, a Mariage Frères tea room from the famous French tea house, and a small garden, The Secret Garden, used as a chill-out corner. Breakfast is praised for its variety and the café's atmosphere.

The real draw here is the location in the heart of Thonglor — out of Soi Sukhumvit 57, it's under a 5-minute walk to BTS Thong Lo, and all around are the restaurants, cafés, bars and community malls that make this one of Bangkok's most popular neighbourhoods. Anyone who loves to eat and go out at night will have a great time without needing to travel far. For Siam or Asok, it's just a few BTS stops away.

To be honest, The Salil Thonglor isn't flawless on every front. Some reviews mention a musty smell in certain rooms, street noise in rooms facing the road, and minor maintenance issues you can still come across. But weighed against rates from around THB 2,800/night, design that punches above its price, and a location that's hard to find in this area, most guests still rate it highly and say they'd return. It scores 8.9 from 1,214 reviews on Trip.com and ranks among the top hotels in Bangkok on TripAdvisor.

A tip from reading many reviews: ask for a room not facing the main street if you're a light sleeper, as Thonglor stays lively late. If you're a couple or want more space, the Living Suite with its separate sitting area is worth the difference. And don't miss the Mariage Frères tea room, or photographing the rooftop pool at sunset.

honestSummary: The Salil Thonglor is at its best for travellers who want good looks and a central Thonglor location at an attainable boutique price — a walk to the BTS, cafés and restaurants all around, and photo-ready corners throughout. Just accept that it has been open for years: some rooms show wear and cleanliness can be hit-or-miss room to room.
honestChecks: If you're a light sleeper sensitive to noise — Thonglor stays lively late and street-facing rooms catch it → ask for a higher floor or an inward-facing room.
If you expect a brand-new hotel in every corner — this opened in 2017 and some rooms show wear with a classic look → if that's not for you, see the newer boutiques in this same roundup.
If you want serious swimming — the rooftop pool is small, better for a dip and photos → for a lap pool, a larger hotel serves you better.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — The Salil Hotel Sukhumvit 57 - Thonglor

faq.q: Where is The Salil Thonglor and how do I get to the BTS?
faq.a: The Salil is at 24 Soi Sukhumvit 57 in Thonglor, Watthana district. It's about a 5-minute walk to BTS Thong Lo, from where Siam, Asok and Phrom Phong are just a few stops away. The hotel is surrounded by Thonglor's restaurants, cafés and community malls.

faq.q: What are the starting prices and room types at The Salil Thonglor?
faq.a: Rates start from approx. THB 2,800/night for a Premier Room (~30 sqm, with a fridge/kitchenette), rising to the Deluxe Suite, The Living Suite (45 sqm, with a separate living area) and the Family Suite. Prices depend on dates and package, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Does The Salil Thonglor have a pool, and what's it like?
faq.a: Yes — a rooftop pool on the 8th floor with views over Thonglor. It isn't large, so it's better for a relaxing dip and evening photos than serious swimming. Reviews say it looks its best at sunset.

faq.q: Who is The Salil Thonglor best suited for?
faq.a: It's ideal for couples, café-lovers and anyone who likes to eat and explore Thonglor. The vintage British design photographs beautifully and the location is a walk from the BTS and top restaurants. It suits travellers after a stylish boutique at an attainable price more than those seeking a full-on luxury hotel or a large pool.

faq.q: Are the rooms at The Salil Thonglor clean and in good condition?
faq.a: Mostly yes, but it varies by room. Many reviews praise the rooms' looks and space, while some mention a musty smell, signs of wear or insects in certain rooms. Since the hotel opened in 2017, it's worth viewing the room at check-in and asking to change if you're not happy.

faq.q: What restaurants and tea rooms does The Salil Thonglor have?
faq.a: There's Bar Storia del Café for coffee and all-day dining, a Mariage Frères tea room from the famous French tea house, and a small garden, The Secret Garden, to relax in. Breakfast is praised for its variety and the café's attractive setting.
